changed.title: Find an eight-gate selector testing membership of one of five rows in a supplied pair
changed.statement:
∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit,
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ C.size ≤ 8 ∧
  ∀ (u a b : Fin 5),
    C.eval (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin 5 => decide (i = u)) ++
      List.ofFn (fun i : Fin 5 => decide (i = a ∨ i = b))) = decide (u = a ∨ u = b)
changed.unlocks: tests whether the explicit nine-gate selector on five labels can be shortened
changed.context: Give a list of at most eight AND/OR gates and an output wire. Wires 0 through 4 select the row and wires 5 through 9 indicate the members of the pair. Check fan-in, size and the 125 triples by finite evaluation. The nine-gate example uses one AND per row and four ORs. Its exact gate list and all evaluations are in methods/find/example-free-column-selector.lean.txt.

changed.title: Zero deletions suffice with an empty shore for the five-by-five pairing atlas representative 25298977
changed.statement:
let G := fun (i j : Fin 5) => (25298977 : ℕ).testBit (5 * i.val + j.val)
let u : ℕ := 0
let t : ℕ := 0
(∃ (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin 5)) (K L : Finset (Fin 5)),
    L ⊆ K ∧ L.card ≤ u ∧ 5 ≤ K.card + t ∧
    ∀ i ∈ K, ∀ j ∈ K,
      Bool.xor (Bool.xor (G i (π i)) (G j (π j))) (Bool.xor (G i (π j)) (G j (π i))) =
      Bool.xor (decide (i ∈ L)) (decide (j ∈ L)))
changed.unlocks: certifies the zero endpoint of the bounded-shore deletion curve for atlas representative 25298977
changed.context: Use column images 3,4,2,1,0 in row order. Retain all five labels and take the empty shore. The ten unordered pairs each have four-corner XOR zero. Diagonal pairs cancel, and reversing the pair preserves parity. This same witness works at every larger shore budget.

changed.statement: PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.HasCircuitSize 9 (fun x : Fin 9 → Bool => (x 0 && x 4 && x 8) || (x 0 && x 5 && x 7) || (x 1 && x 3 && x 8) || (x 1 && x 5 && x 6) || (x 2 && x 3 && x 7) || (x 2 && x 4 && x 6)) 12
changed.unlocks: a lower rung of the ladder for 3 by 3 bipartite perfect matching
changed.context: FIND (beat this), one rung of a ladder at 13, 12 and 11. Your answer is an object: a gate list (AND, OR, NOT, at most two inputs each; wires 0 to 8 are the inputs) and its output wire; decide the equality over all 512 inputs. The best circuit known to us has 14 gates, replayed on every input; whether 12 is possible is unknown to us.

changed.sketch: A calibration of our constructions; no claim attached either way. Answer with a circuit, not an argument: a gate list (operation, wires read; wires 0..n-1 are the input bits in the statement's order, gate j writes wire n+j, each gate reads only earlier wires) and the output wire. Judged by one kernel evaluation over every input. Any search method is welcome; only the circuit is checked. We hold 14 gates with no NOT gate: expand along the first row and share every 2 by 2 minor. Constructions only so far; our solver run at this size did not finish, so we do not know if this bound exists.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 6 bipartite graph with mask 268222 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 9 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 4) (v : Fin 6) => (268222 : ℕ).testBit (6 * u.val + v.val)) 9
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 4 by 6 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 10 AND/OR gates (three plain forms, full lines taken out, equal gates merged and unread gates dropped); at this size those forms are weak; we hold none of 9; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 9 (on paper), a gap of 1. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 3 left, 4 to 9 right, gate j writes wire 10 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 24 inputs with one vertex on each side.

changed.title: Promise-Ball-SAT uses b branches when every initially false clause has at most b variables and width is at most b+1 (known result rebuilt)
changed.statement:
∀ (n b r : Nat), 0 < b →
  let V := Fin n
  let Point := V → Bool
  let Clause := Finset (V × Bool)
  let sat := fun (formula : Finset Clause) (x : Point) =>
    ∀ c ∈ formula, ∃ lit ∈ c, x lit.1 = lit.2
  ∀ (clauses : List Clause) (center : Point),
    let F := clauses.toFinset
    let bad := fun (x : Point) (c : Clause) => ∀ lit ∈ c, x lit.1 ≠ lit.2
    let vars := fun (c : Clause) => c.image Prod.fst
    let state := fun (flipped : Finset V) (v : V) =>
      if v ∈ flipped then !(center v) else center v
    let run := fun (choices : Fin r → Fin b) =>
      (List.finRange r).foldl (fun used step =>
        let c := (clauses.find? (fun d => decide (bad (state used) d))).getD ∅
        let options := ((vars c) \ used).sort (· ≤ ·)
        let picked := options[ (choices step).val ]?
        used ∪ picked.toList.toFinset) (∅ : Finset V)
    (∀ c ∈ F, (vars c).card ≤ b+1) →
    (∀ c ∈ F, bad center c → (vars c).card ≤ b) →
    (∃ y : Point, sat F y ∧ ((Finset.univ : Finset V).filter (fun i => y i ≠ center i)).card ≤ r) ↔
      ∃ choices : Fin r → Fin b, sat F (state (run choices))
changed.unlocks: Prices the local search after restriction on a small disjoint packing of false clauses.
changed.context: Maintain agreement of flipped bits with a chosen nearby model. A false clause has an unflipped variable on which the current word differs from that model. If it was false initially it has at most b variables. If it was true initially, at least one of its at most b+1 variables is already flipped. Hence a valid branch selects the useful variable and reduces distance by one. Once satisfied, all remaining steps are idle. Conversely the procedure flips at most r bits.
